quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: On a slippery road, keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: Your car needs more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Always keep a longer following distance when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Be realistic about travel time, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Honk and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Safety belts:

options.text: Do not need to be worn if your car has airbags.
Only need to be worn on long trips.
Must be worn at all times while the car is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be worn at all times while the car is moving.
questions.explanation: Always wear a safety belt, even on short trips. Most serious crashes happen within 25 miles of home at speeds under 40 mph. Everyone in the car should wear a safety belt, even if the car has airbags.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to finish your turn before the light changes.
You don't need to use your turn signal.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. If you want to turn, get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when turning left. Once the intersection is clear and signals allow, you can complete your turn.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Stop for pedestrians even if there is no crosswalk.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you there faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It doesn't save time and leads to poor decisions while driving.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
This lane must turn right.
Right turns are only allowed on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow-green warning signs alert you to road conditions ahead, such as curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Fewer lanes ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: You should only drive at the maximum posted speed limit when:

options.text: During the night.
During the day.
Conditions are ideal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive when conditions are perfect. Always drive at a safe speed that matches traffic conditions. All drivers must drive safely.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You may go only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first gets the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives second gets the right-of-way.
The driver to your left always gets the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first gets the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, the first driver to arrive gets the right-of-way. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right gets the right-of-way.

questions.question: An instructional permit allows you to:

options.text: Drive while supervised by a licensed driver over 21 years old.
Drive without supervision.
Watch another driver operate a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive while supervised by a licensed driver over 21 years old.
questions.explanation: With an instructional permit, you can drive only when a licensed adult is in the front seat. This adult must be at least 21 years old and have one year of driving experience.

questions.question: When driving on the freeway behind a large truck, you should:

options.text: Drive closer than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
Drive farther back than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
Move to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther back than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay farther behind large trucks because they have larger blind spots.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only yield if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction work areas are:

options.text: Red with green writing.
Orange with black writing.
Yellow with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: You are required to stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.
At a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a red light. Always obey police officers directing traffic, even if traffic signs or signals say something different.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in construction work areas are:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Drive carefully when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner and is about to cross in front of you. What should you do before turning right?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. It is unsafe and illegal to turn right here.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn and drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop and wait until the person with a white cane or guide dog is completely away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: When it rains or is foggy, what headlights should you use to see better?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the water or moisture and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which of these is illegal?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Both actions are illegal. You cannot pass in no passing zones, at railroad crossings, where you cannot see far enough ahead, or at street crossings. You also cannot pass in work zones or when the car ahead has stopped for a pedestrian.
